entry.summary: Delivered the initial Week 3 task brief to Learner A7 outlining context, scope, deliverables, deadline, success standards, and support routing.

actor_messages.text:
Learner A7, you are assigned to complete the Week 3 task for the Video Generation pipeline.

Task Context:
You are responsible for the final stage of the Video Generation pipeline: building a Python workflow to convert the produced HTML file into a valid MP4 video.

What You Must Build:
- A runnable Python workflow that ingests an HTML file and outputs a playable MP4 file.
- Pipeline integration ensuring the workflow cleanly accepts upstream HTML input and outputs the finished video.
- Error logging across the entire codebase that produces actionable log output rather than silent failures.

Required Deliverables:
1. The Python workflow codebase for HTML to MP4 conversion.
2. Full documentation covering both backend and frontend components.
3. A complete README file containing end-to-end setup and execution instructions.
4. A report detailing your error logging strategy and codebase implementation.

Assets:
No external asset files or external repository links are attached to this brief. Use standard pipeline HTML inputs for your workflow.

Deadline:
Thursday, July 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time.

Success Standards:
- The conversion flow must run end-to-end without manual patching and output a playable MP4 file.
- Documentation must be clear enough for another engineer to set up and run the workflow from the README alone.
- Error logging must cover the entire codebase and align with your report.

Support Routing and Submission:
- Final submission: Submit your completed work directly to your mentor prior to the deadline.
- Technical questions and draft reviews: Direct code and technical implementation questions to your mentor.
- Management decisions: Bring scope, priority, or approval matters to me.
- Administrative or access issues: For program or personal matters, contact internship coordinator Nadeen Diaa. For technical access or infrastructure blockers, notify the internship admins in your team group.

The backend is responsible for converting an HTML file into a playable MP4 video.

```

```

---

# Components

## main.py

Application entry point.

Responsibilities:

- Starts the workflow
- Receives input HTML path

---

## workflow.py

Coordinates the complete pipeline.

Responsibilities:

- Validate HTML
- Render HTML
- Capture Frames
- Encode MP4
- Log workflow status

---

## validator.py

Checks input validity.

Responsibilities:

- Verify HTML file exists
- Validate file extension
- Raise validation exceptions

---

## renderer.py

Responsible for rendering the HTML.

Responsibilities:

- Launch Chromium
- Open HTML page
- Capture multiple frames
- Save frames to disk"}, {"id": "docs/frontend.md_0", "content": "# Frontend Documentation

## Overview

The frontend layer consists of the HTML document that will be rendered into a video.

The renderer loads the HTML using Chromium (Playwright), executes CSS and JavaScript, captures the rendered frames, and passes them to the video encoder.

---

# Supported Input

The workflow accepts standard HTML files.

Example

```
input/sample.html
```

---

# HTML Requirements

The HTML document should contain:

- Valid HTML5 structure
- UTF-8 encoding
- Proper `<head>` section
- Proper `<body>` section

Example

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Demo</title>
</head>

<body>

</body>
</html>
```

---

# Supported CSS

The renderer supports standard CSS including:

- Colors
- Fonts
- Flexbox
- Grid
- Positioning
- Backgrounds
- Borders
- Shadows
- Gradients

---

# CSS Animations

Supported animation types include:

- @keyframes
- opacity
- transform
- translate
- rotate
- scale
- transition

Example

```css
@keyframes fade {"}, {"id": "docs/frontend.md_1", "content": "Example

```css
@keyframes fade {

    from {
        opacity:0;
    }

    to{
        opacity:1;
    }

}
```

---

# JavaScript Support

The Chromium renderer executes JavaScript before capturing frames.

Supported features:

- DOM manipulation
- Timers
- CSS animation triggers
- Dynamic rendering

---

# Images

Supported image formats

- PNG
- JPG
- JPEG
- SVG
- GIF (first rendered frame)

---

# Fonts

Supported fonts include:

- Local fonts
- Google Fonts
- Custom web fonts

---

# Resolution

Default viewport

```
1280 × 720
```

The viewport can be modified inside renderer.py.

---

# Output

The frontend produces rendered frames which are passed to the encoder.

```
HTML

↓

Rendered Page

↓

Frames

↓

MP4
```

---

# Best Practices

- Use responsive layouts.
- Avoid extremely large images.
- Keep JavaScript lightweight.
- Verify assets exist before rendering."}]}, {"rubric_id": 10, "status": "Partial", "chunks_ids_met": ["README.md_1", "docs/logging_report.md_2"], "reason": "Logging is present and partially documented, but the report does not fully explain the logging strategy or match the code in detail.", "confidence_score": 0.7, "evaluation_criteria": "Avoided: logging spans the whole code and is well documented in the report.", "chunks_met": [{"id": "README.md_1", "content": "---

### 1. `asset_service/asset.py` (The Data Validation Layer)

Learner A2, you are assigned to Sprint 4 — Task 6: Docker Research, Team Knowledge Share & Containerisation.

Task Context
You are tasked with conducting Docker research, onboarding your team on containerisation methodology, and setting up container configuration for the project.

What You Must Build or Analyze

+# Local Setup Guide — Running the Project with Docker
+
+**Branch:** `feature/mahdi-docker-setup`
+
+This guide walks you through running the full backend + frontend stack locally using
+Docker, without installing Python or Node dependencies directly on your machine.
+
+## 1. Prerequisites
+
+- [Docker Desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/) installed and running
+  (you'll see the whale icon in your system tray/menu bar when it's up)
+- Git
+
+That's it — you don't need Python, Node, or any of the project's libraries installed
+locally. Docker handles all of that inside the containers.
+
+## 2. Clone the repo and switch to this branch
+
+```bash
+git clone https://github.com/anon-github-user/ai-video-generation-app.git
+cd ai-video-generation-app
+git checkout <this-branch-name>
+```
+
+## 3. Create your `.env` file
+
+Copy the example file and fill in your own keys:
+
+```bash
+cp .env.example .env
+```

Learner A2, you are assigned to complete the Workflow Routing & Observability Foundation task for this sprint.

**Task Overview**
You are required to build and instrument the orchestration layer of our automated technical-video-generation system. Wire the Research, Script, Code, and Visual-Plan agents into a single StateGraph with conditional edges, manage shared context within a token budget, implement retry-and-loop transitions capped at MAX_RETRIES, and enforce clean field-ownership. Additionally, instrument the entire pipeline end-to-end with LangSmith tracing and build a Streamlit trace viewer to render the agent decision timeline, latency, token usage, and estimated cost.

**Required Deliverables**
Submit a complete code repository and report containing the following structure:
- Root: .env.example, requirements.txt, design_and_observability_notes.md
- src/: state.py, router.py, context_utils.py, langsmith_config.py, constants.py, graph.py
- agents/: research_agent.py, script_agent.py, code_agent.py, visual_plan_agent.py, llm_client.py
- ui/: trace_viewer.py
- tests/: test_router.py, test_observability.py

**Reference Assets**
- LangGraph Documentation: https://langchain-ai.github.io/langgraph/
- LangSmith Documentation: https://docs.smith.chain.com/
- Streamlit Documentation: https://docs.streamlit.io/

**Deadline & Support**
- Deadline: Thursday, June 18, 2026, 11:59 PM GMT+3 (Africa/Cairo). I expect this by the deadline.
- Support Routing: Technical questions and draft feedback go to your mentor, Sarah Nader. Final submissions must be delivered directly to Sarah for formal review. Do not send drafts or submissions to me.

Review the requirements and begin immediately.

actor_messages.text:
SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
You are an experienced instructional designer and storyboard artist.
You specialise in creating engaging MOOC‑style educational videos.
You understand multimedia learning principles and know how to avoid overwhelming the learner.
You introduce visuals exactly when they become relevant in the narration.
You never generate assets yourself; you only reference existing assets or create text cues.
""".strip()

TASK_TEMPLATE = """
You are given the following script for an educational video:

Video ID: {video_id}
Title: {title}
Total Duration: {total_duration_seconds} seconds

Narration Segments:
{segments}

Word Timestamps:
{word_timestamps}

Available Visual Assets:
{assets}

---

Your job is to create a storyboard for the animation engine.

For every narration segment:
- Decide whether a new scene is required.
- Select an appropriate layout.
- Decide which visual elements appear.
- Decide when every element should appear.
- Use word triggers whenever the narration explicitly introduces a concept.
- Otherwise use segment_start.

Rules:
- You MUST generate at least 7 scenes. If the script is short, create transitional scenes (e.g., title, summary, transition) or split longer segments to reach 7 scenes.
- Every scene must reference one or more script segments.
- Every visual cue must reference exactly one segment.
- Every visual cue MUST have a valid element_type: one of "text", "image", "diagram", "icon", "gif", "video", "svg". NEVER use "animation", "background", "interactive", or other values.
- Every visual cue MUST have a valid preferred_region: one of "top", "bottom", "left", "right", "center", "background", "top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left", "bottom-right", "middle".
- Use only assets provided in the assets input.
- If no asset exists, create a text cue instead.
- Avoid clutter.
- Prefer one primary visual and at most two secondary visuals.
- Visuals must reinforce the narration rather than duplicate it.
- Keep layouts consistent across consecutive scenes whenever possible.
- Return only the JSON object matching the schema.

IMPORTANT: You MUST base your scenes strictly on the provided segments, title, and assets. Do not invent new topics or use examples not given.
""".strip()

RETRY_PROMPT = """
Your previous response did not conform to the required JSON schema.
Error details: {error}
Please correct the output and return only valid JSON matching the ScenePlan schema.
Do not include any extra text.
""".strip()

REVISION_TEMPLATE = """
You are given:

- Original Script (for context):
{script}

- Original Scene Plan (the one to be revised):
{scene_plan}

- Scene Quality Report (machine‑readable revision instructions):
{quality_report}

The Quality Report contains a list of revision instructions.
Each instruction specifies:
- `target_path` – a JSON‑pointer‑like path to the field that must change.
- `operation` – one of `replace`, `add`, `remove`.
- `new_value` – the new value (only for `replace` and `add`).

Your responsibility is to update the Scene Plan by applying only these instructions.

Rules:
Ensure the final scene plan has at least 7 scenes. If the revision instructions would reduce the count below 7, you must add additional scenes as needed.
- Modify ONLY the fields referenced by the revision instructions.
- Preserve every other field exactly as it is.
- Do NOT regenerate the storyboard.
- Do NOT create additional scenes.
- Do NOT remove scenes.
- Do NOT change scene ordering.
- Do NOT modify scene IDs.
- Do NOT modify cue IDs unless explicitly instructed.
- Every visual cue MUST have a valid element_type: one of "text", "image", "diagram", "icon", "gif", "video", "svg". NEVER use "animation", "background", "interactive", or other values.
- Every visual cue MUST have a valid preferred_region: one of "top", "bottom", "left", "right", "center", "background", "top-left", "top-right", "bottom-left", "bottom-right", "middle".
- Return a complete, schema‑valid ScenePlan JSON.
- Ensure the final output is a valid JSON object matching the ScenePlan schema.

Important: If a `target_path` points to a field that does not exist, skip that instruction and log a warning (but do not raise an error – just ignore it and continue).
""".strip()

# Director / quality checker prompt
# ... existing prompts ...

DIRECTOR_TASK_TEMPLATE = """
You are given:
- Original Script: {script}
- Generated Scene Plan: {scene_plan}

Analyze the Scene Plan and identify any issues that could affect educational quality.

For each issue:
- Provide a clear description.
- Assign a severity: critical, major, or minor.
- Suggest a concrete revision instruction (target_path, operation, new_value).

Also list the strengths of the plan.

Return ONLY a JSON object with the following structure:
{{
  "strengths": ["list of strengths"],
  "revision_instructions": [
    {{
      "instruction_id": "unique_id",
      "severity": "critical|major|minor",
      "issue_type": "one_of: missing_scene, missing_segment, layout_issue, visual_issue, consistency_issue, schema_issue, educational_issue",
      "target_path": "JSON path",
      "operation": "replace|add|remove",
      "new_value": null or value,
      "reason": "why this is an issue",
      "recommendation": "what to do"
    }}
  ]
}}
Do NOT include scores or category scores – these will be computed automatically.
""".strip()

الـ prompt templates الجديدة في `planner.py` طالعة مظبوطة وكاملة جداً دلوقتي. إنك ضفت explicit constraints لـ `element_type` و `preferred_region` و JSON pointer paths في `REVISION_TEMPLATE` و `DIRECTOR_TASK_TEMPLATE` دي خطوة هتخلي الـ revision loop محكومة ومظبوطة أكتر.

اعمل دلوقتي test execution سريع ورن sample script على الـ pipeline، وابعتلي الـ scene plan JSON اللي هيطلع أو snippet صغيرة منه عشان نتأكد شكل الـ outputs بتاعة الـ agent عامل إزاي عملياً.

The Scene Planner stage of the pipeline outputs a ScenePlan — a structured JSON document describing a video's scenes, the narration text for each, and the visual cues (text, images, diagrams, icons, gifs, videos, svgs) that should appear during each scene, along with their preferred screen region and importance. feedback.summary: The PR successfully refines asset prompts to 2D vector style and integrates Pollinations.ai (FLUX) to avoid Gemini quota limits. However, it lacks an explicit visual quality evaluation comparing initial vs improved outputs, and does not demonstrate coordination with Learner A3.
feedback.mentor_reply:
شغل عالي في الـ PR وإضافة الـ prompts الجديدة بصيغة 2D vector، وحلو جداً إنك جربت open-source model زي FLUX عن طريق Pollinations عشان تطلع بره limits بتاعة Gemini.

عشان نأكد على الـ visual assets collection بشكل كامل، محتاجين نظبط حاجتين:
الأولى إنك توثق visual quality evaluation بسيط يوضح الفرق بين الصور القديمة والجديدة وليه التعديل ده فرق في الجودة، والثانية إنك تشارك المقارنة دي مع مصطفى باهي وتتفقوا سوا على النتيجة.

مش لازم كل حاجة تبقى هندرد بيرسنت، ابعت الـ visual outputs دي لمصطفى في الـ text chat، وحط ملخص المقارنة في الـ PR عشان نعتمد الشغل على طول.

Once you add that evaluation summary to the PR, let me know so we can wrap this up!

Learner A3,

You are assigned to build a Scene Quality Check Agent to evaluate narrative or production scenes for completeness and consistency.

**Agent Requirements**
Your agent must perform the following functions:
- Define a structured and actionable scene quality rubric.
- Detect missing, ambiguous, or inconsistent scene information.
- Score scene quality based on your defined rubric.
- Generate logical, constructive improvement feedback.

**Required Deliverables**
Submit the complete source code, the defined quality rubric, and test outputs demonstrating evaluations of sample scenes. No external assets or starter datasets are provided; you must construct your own test scenarios to demonstrate performance.

**Success Standard**
To meet the required professional standard, your agent must successfully parse a scene, accurately flag deficiencies, generate logical scores, and provide clear, actionable feedback aligned with your rubric.

**Deadline**
I expect this by the deadline of Tuesday, July 21, 2026, at 3:11 PM Cairo time. Prompt delivery is expected.

**Support Routing**
Send technical implementation questions, code troubleshooting, and draft reviews to your mentor. Direct scope approvals, deadline issues, and final milestone inquiries to me. Begin immediately.

Learner A4, welcome to Sprint 4. Below is your official task brief and operational expectations for this sprint.

**Task Context:**
Sprint 4 — Task 1: Script Generation Prompt Enhancement.
You are assigned to enhance the prompt of the agent that converts a simple idea into a video script. The objective is to ensure the generated script becomes materially richer and more detailed, clearly explaining underlying concepts rather than skimming over them.

**What You Must Build:**
- Rewrite and enhance the script-generation agent's system prompt to produce detailed, concept-explaining scripts from simple input ideas.
- Ensure the prompt generalizes across various topics rather than being hardcoded to a single demo idea.
- Maintain coherent structure and sequencing so the generated script remains fully usable for downstream scene planning.
- Commit the updated prompt directly to the project repository.

**Required Deliverables:**
- The updated script-generation prompt committed to the repository.
- Before and after sample scripts generated from the exact same input idea, clearly demonstrating the improvement in depth and explanatory quality.

**Assets and Links:**
- No external asset links are provided for this task. Work directly within your assigned codebase.

**Deadline:**
- Friday, August 7, 2026 at 2:59 AM Cairo time.

**Success Standard:**
- Demonstrable, material improvement in output quality between the before and after scripts using an identical input topic, with explicit prompt instructions enforcing clarity, depth, and structural validity for downstream integration.

**Support and Submission Routing:**
- Submit your completed deliverable directly to your mentor prior to the deadline.
- Technical implementation questions, draft prompt feedback, and task execution support must be routed to your mentor.
- Administrative, personal, access, or program-level questions must be directed to the internship group admins in the team channel.

Review these requirements and proceed with execution.

أحمد، رجعت لـ `main-branch-documentation.md` وقريتها كاملة. أول حاجة: التوثيق ده مبني على الكود الفعلي مش على الخطة القديمة، وده بالظبط اللي كان مطلوب. توصيف الـ pipeline بمراحله الخمسة، والـ DB schema، والـ endpoint specs، والفصل الواضح بين الـ real code والـ dummy functions — كل ده سليم ودقيق.
وأهم نقطة عملتها صح: إنك وثّقت الـ architecture pivot بوضوح — إن `docs/architecture.md` القديم بيقول 8 مراحل backend، بينما الكود الحقيقي بيشغّل 5 بس والـ Composition والـ Animation والـ Render اتنقلوا للـ frontend. توثيق الفرق بين المكتوب والواقع ده أنضف من إنك تسيبه ساكت.
فاضل 4 حاجات من الملاحظات اللي بعتهالك قبل كده، محتاج أتأكد إنها اتقفلت:
`docs/architecture.md` نفسه — لازم يتحدّث فعلياً عشان يعكس الـ pivot، مش بس نشاور عليه إنه out of sync. أي حد جديد هيقرا الملف ده الأول وهيبني على معلومة غلط.
`docs/api.md` — لسه template فاضي. المحتوى موجود عندك بالفعل في التوثيق، محتاج بس ينتقل مكانه الصح.
قرار من عمر درغام على `composition_data` و `animation_data`: هيتشالوا ولا هيفضلوا كـ legacy columns؟ لازم القرار نفسه يتكتب في الدوك مش بس ينتظر.
مجلد `render/` (104K، أكبر مجلد في الباك اند) — محتاج سطر واحد على الأقل يقول هو لسه live بعد الـ pivot ولا بقى dead code.
والحاجة الأخيرة اللي طلبتها المرة اللي فاتت: الـ frontend UI structure محتاج تغطية أعمق — الـ components إيه، وكل واحد بيتكلم مع أنهي endpoint، وإزاي ده بيتربط بكود عمر. ده الجزء اللي هيحتاجه أي حد داخل على المشروع بعدك.
الحاجات دي كلها polish مش rework. اقفلهم وابعتلي، وأنا أكمّل من هناك.

Login/registration forms with Supabase Auth client + session persistence

 — the Supabase Auth client

Learner A3, you are assigned to build the Scene Quality Check Agent. This task must be delivered to a professional standard by the deadline.

**Task Context**
The objective is to establish an automated Scene Quality Check Agent. Consistent scene metadata and quality control are essential in production environments. You are responsible for designing and implementing an agentic workflow that evaluates scene quality based on structured criteria.

**What You Must Build**
Develop an agent that performs the following core functions:
1. Define a clear, structured quality rubric for evaluating scene data.
2. Detect missing, incomplete, or inconsistent information within scene descriptions.
3. Calculate and assign a quantitative quality score to each scene based on your rubric.
4. Generate actionable improvement feedback for scenes that do not meet standard benchmarks.

**Required Deliverables**
Your submission must include:
- Complete source code implementing the quality check agent and the evaluation rubric.
- Detailed documentation explaining the implementation, rubric structure, and instructions on how to run the agent.
- Output logs or test cases demonstrating the agent evaluating and scoring scenes and producing feedback.

**Assets and Links**
No pre-defined assets or external datasets are provided. You must design and generate your own test cases and evaluation scenarios to validate your implementation.

**Deadline**
The firm deadline for this deliverable is Thursday, July 23, 2026, at 11:59 PM Cairo time. Manage your time appropriately. I expect this by the deadline.

**Success Standard**
The deliverable will be evaluated on the completeness and robustness of the agent's logic, the utility of the defined quality rubric, the accuracy of its detection capabilities, and the quality of the generated feedback.

**Support Routing**
For all technical questions, implementation guidance, or draft feedback, consult your mentor. Do not contact me for technical execution details.

okay, you said:
Hi Learner A4 — reviewed the asset lane and ran your test locally (offline, with CrewAI stubbed). The resolver logic and async design are genuinely solid, and there are a few changes worth making — one of them matters for the handoff to Nada. Here's the rundown.
What's working well:
Clean, typed AssetItem / AssetResponseContract schema, and your populate_by_name=True claim checks out on input — I confirmed the contract accepts both assets=[...] and items=[...] with no validation error.
The resolver is nicely engineered: process_scene_elements fans out over cues with asyncio.gather for real concurrency, and offloading the blocking crew.kickoff() to run_in_executor so it doesn't stall the event loop is a great touch. The LLM try/except fallback and empty-input guard are the right safety nets. 👏
Changes to make (in priority order):
1. The alias only works on input — your handoff to Nada will emit the wrong keys. This is the important one. You aliased assets→items, asset_license→license, scene_reference→scene_id "because that's what Nada's Stage 6 expects," but nothing serializes with by_alias=True, and I confirmed Pydantic's default model_dump() emits the field names, not the aliases:
default → {"assets": [...]}, with asset_license / scene_reference
by_alias=True → {"items": [...]}, with license / scene_id
So if you hand Nada JSON, she gets assets/scene_reference/asset_license, not the items/scene_id/license you designed for — a silent mismatch, and "zero validation issues" won't hold on her end. Confirm the boundary with Nada: if it's JSON, serialize with by_alias=True; if she consumes the Pydantic object directly, that's fine but document it. (Cleanest option: make the field names match what she expects and drop the aliases.)
2. Your test doesn't actually prove the LLM works, and it hits the network. test_asset_lane_flow_and_contract calls the real CrewAI + Gemini with no mock, so "100% green" depends on a live key and network — and the fallback prompt ("Illustration showing: ...") also passes both your assertions (len > 0, != cue), so the test goes green even when the LLM call fails. Mock crew.kickoff (or getllm_client) so it's deterministic and offline, and add a test that forces the exception and asserts the fallback prompt specifically — that way you're testing both paths.
3. Import rooting + branch is behind main. Everything uses absolute from backend.app... imports, which only resolve when the repo root is on the path — other lanes use app.schemas... / models..., so align the import root with the team. Also your branch is well behind current main (main now has services/, models/, routes/, main.py your branch doesn't include), so rebase onto latest main before merging or the diff will be messy.
4. Minor: registered_at is a hardcoded "2026-07-15T12:00:00Z" — use datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(). And in the AssetItem(...) constructor you mix an alias (license=) with a field name (scene_reference=); pick one for consistency.
Bottom line — ~3.5/5, strong core that needs the handoff and test fixes before it's merge-ready. The async resolver and schema are good work; the must-fixes are the by_alias serialization (so Nada actually gets items/scene_id), a mocked test that distinguishes real-LLM output from the fallback, and rebasing onto current main with consistent imports. Do those and it's a clean pass. Let me know if you'd like me to draft the corrected test and the exact serialization change. 🙌

Seeing the code makes the issue much clearer. To handle the serialization, you'll want to call `model_dump(by_alias=True)` on your contract instance so the exported keys align perfectly with what's expected in Stage 6.

For your test suite, you can mock the CrewAI kickoff using `unittest.mock.patch` to return a clean string for the normal flow, and then set it to raise an exception to verify your fallback path. 👍

```python
# In your response logic:
json_data = contract.model_dump(by_alias=True)

# In test_assets.py:
from unittest.mock import patch

with patch("backend.app.services.resolver.Crew.kickoff") as mock_kickoff:
    mock_kickoff.return_value = "Mocked image description"
    # test normal flow
    
    mock_kickoff.side_effect = Exception("API error")
    # test fallback flow
```

Learner A4, here is your kickoff brief for Sprint 4.

Task Context
You are assigned to Sprint 4 - User Authentication. Your objective is to build an end-to-end authentication layer across the backend and frontend on top of the existing UI. You will integrate Supabase Auth and establish strict multi-tenant data isolation for user videos.

What You Must Build
- Login and signup UI components integrated with authentication API endpoints.
- Supabase Auth integration for registration, login, session tokens, and password handling.
- A dedicated users database table in Supabase linked via foreign keys to the video table.
- Row Level Security (RLS) policies in Supabase ensuring authenticated users can only view and manage their own generated videos.

Required Deliverables
1. Repository code updates committed under src/auth/ and supabase/migrations/.
2. Documentation containing the following required sections:

- No external asset files are required. You will integrate directly with the existing project repository and UI schema.

Deadline
- Friday, August 7, 2026, at 2:59:59 AM Cairo time. Deliverables must be completed and ready on schedule; scope swaps and deadline extensions are declined.

Success Standard
- Functional registration and login flow via UI forms with proper session persistence and route protection.
- Committed Supabase migration scripts establishing explicit foreign keys between user profiles and video records.
- Verified Row Level Security (RLS) policies enforcing complete data isolation across users.

Support & Routing
- Technical implementation questions, code troubleshooting, and draft feedback must be directed to your mentor.
- Administrative, platform access, or program operational questions must be directed to the internship group admins in your team group.
- Scope approvals, timeline accountability, and final milestone sign-off remain under my ownership.

Learner A6 — actually opened both files you sent (docker_output.html, html_code_writer.py). Detailed feedback:
docker_output.html: this is a real, complete rendered frame — proper glassmorphism panel styling, a full keyframe animation set (fadeUp, popIn, slideInLeft/Right, float/floatReverse/pulseSoft), progress dots, and your 3 required animation classes (float, float-reverse, pulse-soft) are all present and wired to actual @keyframes rather than just named and unused. This confirms the template-to-final-output path genuinely works, not just in theory.
html_code_writer.py:
Good resilience design — it tries CrewAI + Gemini first for intelligent placeholder-filling, and falls back to direct Jinja2 rendering if the LLM call fails for any reason, which you correctly noted always works since the templates are already valid Jinja2. That fallback is exactly the right safety net for a pipeline stage that shouldn't be allowed to hard-fail.
One real bug: normalize_model_name() defaults to "gemini/gemini-3.5-flash-lite" and populate_scene_template() defaults MODEL_NAME to "gemini/gemini-3.5-flash" if the env var isn't set — neither of those is a real Gemini model identifier (the actual lineup is versions like 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, etc.). If MODEL_NAME isn't set in your .env, every LLM call will fail against the real API and you'll silently fall onto the Jinja2 fallback every single time without realizing the LLM path isn't actually running. Fix the default model string to a real one.
The prompt guardrails for the LLM are well written (don't invent assets, don't touch layout/CSS, keep animation classes, raw HTML only) and you defensively strip markdown fences and stray Jinja comments from the LLM output before returning it — good, since LLMs reliably ignore "no markdown" instructions some percentage of the time.
To close out the deliverable (matching what Sarah already outlined): wire this into the integration wrapper function so Learner A4 can import and call the whole pipeline end to end, and once that's connected, run one real end-to-end test to confirm scene_plan.json -> populated templates -> final merged HTML renders and animates cleanly with zero runtime errors. feedback.summary: Reviewed submitted pipeline files (orchestrator.py, html_code_writer.py, and 4 layout templates). The template modularity is solid. Key areas for improvement include exposing a single wrapper entry-point function for integration handoff and verifying the LiteLLM model string to ensure active generation of inline CSS/JS animations.
feedback.mentor_reply:
I reviewed the submitted files, including orchestrator.py, html_code_writer.py, and your four layout templates (template_intro, template_outro, template_content_a, template_content_b). The modular template architecture and fallbacks are structured nicely.

To polish this for final integration, ensure orchestrator.py exposes a single callable wrapper function with a clear input/output contract ready for handoff. Also verify that your LiteLLM model string in html_code_writer.py points to a valid model so the active LLM generation path runs cleanly with fully inlined CSS and JavaScript animations without falling back silently.

Run an end-to-end pipeline test from scene plan JSON to the final animated HTML output, confirm there are no rendering errors, and let me know if you run into any blockers as you wrap it up.

actor_messages.text: دي كل الملفات كدا

بصيت على الفايلات اللي بعتها، orchestrator.py و html_code_writer.py والـ layout templates بتوعك (template_intro و template_outro و template_content_a و template_content_b). الـ modular template architecture والـ fallbacks متظبطين ومتقسمين بشكل نضيف جداً.

عشان نقفل الجزء ده للـ final integration، محتاجين نركز على نقطتين:
- تأكد إن orchestrator.py بيدينا single callable wrapper function واضحة بـ input/output contract محدد جاهز للـ handoff.
- راجع الـ LiteLLM model string في html_code_writer.py وتأكد إنه بيشاور على موديل شغال صح، عشان الـ active LLM generation يطلع inlined CSS و JavaScript animations مضبوطة من غير ما ينزل على الـ fallback سايلنت.

اعمل end-to-end pipeline test كامل من الـ scene plan JSON لحد الـ animated HTML output النهائي، وتأكد إن مفيش أي rendering errors. ولو واجهتك أي مشكلة وأنت بتقفلها ابعتلي.

Practical fix for the actual cause: 100k tokens in under 2 hours for troubleshooting usually means the full context (logs, file contents, prior turns) is getting re-sent on every single call. entry.summary: Guided the learner on using an abstracted, swappable TTS interface with OpenAI or mock providers.

actor_messages.text: which API should I use for audio generation ?

Hi Learner A2! 👋 For the audio generation stage, the main thing is ensuring your text-to-speech engine is abstracted and swappable rather than tied to just one vendor.

If you are looking for a straightforward API integration, OpenAI's TTS API with models like `tts-1` and voices like `alloy` or `nova` is a solid option. In your `backend/app/services/tts_provider.py`, you'll want to define an abstract base provider interface. This lets you run an `OpenAITTSProvider` for production and a local `MockTTSProvider` for your `pytest` suite, which saves you from making live network calls and running up API costs while testing.

Whichever API you go with, just make sure the provider supports selectable voices and speaking rates, and fits cleanly with the `AudioTrack` schema. I'm happy to help you sketch out that interface structure if you'd like to map it out together.

entry.summary: Clarified the difference between Google Cloud TTS and Gemini API for the voiceover task.

actor_messages.text: you mean Google Cloud Text-to-Speech API or Gemini API

Google Cloud Text-to-Speech is a dedicated speech synthesis API, whereas Gemini is primarily a multimodal LLM. For this voiceover task, a dedicated engine like Google Cloud TTS or OpenAI's TTS is the standard choice for handling voice synthesis and speaking rates. Whichever you decide to go with, just make sure it is implemented behind your abstract interface in `tts_provider.py` so we can easily swap them out later.
